title: p-adic comparison theorems
summary: Results classed as known in the literature and missing from Mathlib, proved here with their own definitions.

modules.title: Derived completeness, adic approximation of comparisons and completed base change
modules.note:
This file shows that comparison maps of cohomology are bijective, by reduction modulo a scalar and
successive approximation. `New.Variety.H N F n` is `Extⁿ(N, F)` in the category `AbFunctor C` of
functors `C ⥤ Ab`. `New.Variety.moduleCoeff Φ` is a module-valued functor `Φ` (`act a` is
multiplication by `a` on it, `push N q n` is the map on `Hⁿ` induced by `q`, and `a • x` on `Hⁿ` is
`push N (act a) n x`), read as such a functor of coefficients.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.IsDerivedComplete`: derived π-completeness, the bijectivity of `New.shiftDiff π` on
  sequences. It passes to powers `ι → X`, to retracts up to a power of π, to cohomology
  (`New.Variety.IsDerivedComplete.cohomology`) and, in finite rank, to base change
  (`New.Variety.IsDerivedComplete.baseChange`).
* `New.Variety.Comparison.IsBijective.of_mod`: a comparison of complete cohomology groups that is
  bijective modulo `a` is bijective.
* `New.Variety.IsCompletionBijective`, `New.Variety.moduleCompletionIso`: linear maps that are
  bijective on p-adic completions, and the p-adic completion of an algebra, as a module.
* `New.Variety.HasFlatBaseChange.isBijective_of_isReductionMod`: `Hⁿ(N, S ⊗ Θ) → Hⁿ(N, X)` is
  bijective if `S ⊗ Θ → X` is so modulo p. The cohomology of `N` must commute with flat base change.
  `W` must be a discrete valuation ring with uniformiser p, and `S` must be flat over `W`. The lemma
  also needs completeness and no p-torsion of `W`, `S` and every value of `Θ` and `X`, and finite
  rank of `Hⁿ(N, Θ)` for each n where the kernel of the map on `Hⁿ` is p-divisible.

Notions from other files:
* `New.shiftDiff`: The operator (x_j) ↦ (x_j − π x_{j+1}) on sequences in a module.
* `New.Variety.Comparison.IsBijective`: For a functor φ: C' → C, a map β: F∘φ → F' and α: N' → N∘φ,
  the map Ext^n(N, F) → Ext^n(N', F') is bijective for every n.
* `New.Variety.IsReductionMod`: The map f is surjective, and f(x) = 0 exactly when x is a multiple
  m·y of m.
* `New.Variety.HasFlatBaseChange`: a functor N to abelian groups has it if M ⊗_S Hⁿ(N, Φ) → Hⁿ(N, M
  ⊗_S Φ) is bijective for all n, all functors Φ to S-modules and all S-flat M.
* `New.Variety.Comparison.restrict`: The cohomological comparison datum along a functor φ: C' → C
  from an abelian-group-valued functor N to N∘φ, with identity coefficient map.
modules.literature:
Known result: Derived completeness for a principal ideal, covering Nakayama, finiteness and
completed base change. Only modules and Ext groups are treated, and completeness is defined as
bijectivity of x_n - a x_(n+1) on sequences. Base change is proved for modules of finite rank over a
discrete valuation ring, with bounded torsion shown by hand. Source: Stacks Project 091N, 091P,
0G1U, 09BA, 0CQY; B. Bhatt, Torsion completions are bounded, JPAA (2019); L. Positselski,
Contraadjusted modules, contramodules, and reduced cotorsion modules, arXiv 1605.03934.

modules.title: Wang sequence on C × Bℕ, lines, and root systems of units via periodic sequences
modules.note:
Write Bℕ for the one-object category of the monoid ℕ. A functor on C × Bℕ (`New.Variety.TimesBNat`)
is a functor Y on C with an endomorphism γ. Its cohomology plays the part of that of the homotopy
quotient by γ. Cohomology is Hⁿ(Y, F) = Extⁿ(ℤ[Y], F) in functors to abelian groups. Y is a line
over a functor U on C (`New.Variety.IsLine`) if a map from Y to U is bijective on cohomology. Root
systems of a unit are defined on O_C-algebras, twisted by the character s ↦ (ε^s)^♯. For a unit `v`
of a `p`-adic test (`New.Variety.PadicTest`: its ring `ProdRing` is a product of cells `Cell j`,
`TiltRing` is its tilt, and `algFunctor` sends it to `ProdRing` as an O_C-algebra), they form a line
for the coefficients `tilt ⋙ moduleCoeff (tensorCoeff M)`, provided `moduleCoeff (tensorCoeff M)` is
acyclic on perfect rings (`New.Variety.IsAcyclicOnPerfect`). This is proved by representing them,
through tilting, by the ring of periodic sequences. There the twist becomes the shift.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.TimesBNat.shortExact_wangComplex`: the short exact sequence
  0 → ℤ[Y × ℕ] → ℤ[Y × ℕ] → ℤ[Y] → 0 (`New.Variety.TimesBNat.wangComplex`;
  `New.Variety.TimesBNat.shortExact_induced` is the same with the two maps written out). Its long
  exact sequence is the Wang sequence, since Y × ℕ on C × Bℕ has the cohomology of Y on C
  (`New.Variety.TimesBNat.isLine_fst`).
* `New.Variety.IsLine.of_acyclic`: a criterion for Y to be a line over a representable functor
  Hom(A, −), in terms of the kernel and cokernel of γ - 1 on coefficients
  (`New.Variety.KoszulExact`).
* `New.Variety.compatibleRoots`: A ↦ characters ℚ≥0 → A, that is, elements with a compatible system
  of n-th roots for all n ≥ 1.
* `New.Variety.CompatibleRootsAreLines`: the property of coefficients F and a functor ψ to
  O_C-algebras that the root systems of every unit of every ψ(A) form a line (`New.Variety.IsLine`)
  over Hom(A, −).
* `New.Variety.periodicSeq.koszulExact_shift`: in characteristic `p`, the constants contain the
  kernel of the shift minus the identity, and this map is onto (`New.Variety.KoszulExact`). This
  also holds after tensoring with a module.
* `New.Variety.PadicTest.isLine_compatibleRoots`: if `moduleCoeff (tensorCoeff M)` is acyclic on
  perfect rings (`New.Variety.IsAcyclicOnPerfect`), root systems of `v` have flat base change
  (`New.Variety.HasFlatBaseChange`) and form a line (`New.Variety.IsLine`) for the coefficients
  `tilt ⋙ moduleCoeff (tensorCoeff M)`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.freeAb`: The functor sending a set-valued functor Y to ℤ[Y], whose value at A is the
  free abelian group on Y(A).
* `New.OC`: The ring of integers O_C of the field C_p of p-adic complex numbers.
* `New.Period.OFlat`: The ring O^♭, the inverse limit of O_C/p along x ↦ x^p, where O_C is the ring
  of integers of C_p.
modules.literature:
Known result: Faltings' toric towers and their Koszul complexes. Here the variables are treated one
at a time, and the discrete monoid generated by one automorphism replaces continuous cohomology of
Z_p^d, so that Wang sequences replace the Koszul complex. Source: P. Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory
for rigid-analytic varieties, Forum Math. Pi 1 (2013), Lemmas 4.5 and 5.5; Bhatt, Morrow, Scholze
2018, Lemma 7.3; Stacks project, tag 0EBS; G. Faltings, p-adic Hodge theory, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 1
(1988).

modules.title: Crystallinity of p-adic cohomology of charted proper schemes and Frobenius congruences. Its head has an overview of the theory.
modules.note:
The `p`-adic cohomology `New.Variety.ellAdicCohom` of a proper scheme `Y` is crystalline when `Y` is
charted (`New.Variety.IsCharted`) over a noetherian ring `R` that maps into the valuation ring of a
`p`-adic place of `Ω`, and over `Ω`. A congruence relation Σ n_i [Frob^{a_i} u_i(x)] = 0 between
maps of proper schemes (`New.Variety.CongruenceRelation`) gives the same relation between the
operators on `New.Period.Bmax ⊗ Vⁿ(Y)`.

## Overview of this theory

Let `R` be a commutative ring and `Ω` a fixed algebraic closure of `ℚ` that is an `R`-algebra. Call
a scheme charted over a ring if it is built from charts étale over tori (`New.Variety.IsCharted`).
Let `Vⁿ(Y)` be `New.Variety.ellAdicCohom` for `ℓ = p`, that is, `ℚ_p ⊗ Hⁿ(Y_Ω, ℤ_p)`. A place above
`p` is given by a valuation ring `A` of `Ω` containing the image of `R`.

* `New.Variety.finite_and_primitive_comparison`: let `Y` be proper over `R` and charted over an
  algebraically closed field `Ω` mapping to `ℂ_p`. Let `M` be a module over the tilt `O♭` of
  `O_{ℂ_p}`, with `B ↦ B ⊗ M` acyclic along tilting at perfect `O♭`-algebras. Then the cohomology of
  `Y_Ω` commutes with flat extension of coefficients, and each `Hⁿ(Y_Ω, 𝔽_p)` is finite. If also `R`
  maps compatibly to `O_{ℂ_p}`, the cohomology of `Y_Ω` with coefficients (locally constant `O♭`)
  `⊗ M` maps bijectively to that of `S ↦ Y(S)`. Here `S` runs over the `p`-adic test rings
  (`New.Variety.PadicTest`), with coefficients `S♭ ⊗ M`.
* `New.Variety.exists_period_map`: let `R` map to `O_{ℂ_p}` compatibly with an embedding `Ω → ℚ̄_p`.
  Let `S` be a `p`-torsion-free, `p`-adically complete `A_inf`-algebra and `K` a flat `S`-algebra
  over `ℚ_p`, as in `IsPeriodRingPair`. There are `K`-linear maps from `K ⊗ Vⁿ(Y)` to `Hⁿ` of
  `T ↦ Y(T)` on test rings `T`, with coefficients built from `K` and `W(T♭)`. These maps are natural
  and Galois-compatible. They are bijective when `Y` is proper and charted over `Ω`.
* `New.Variety.ellAdicCohom.isCrystalline_and_linearFrob_rel`: let `R` be noetherian, `K` a field,
  and `Y` proper and charted over `R` and over `Ω`. Then the decomposition group of `A` over `K`
  acts crystallinely on `Vⁿ(Y)`. Let `W` be proper and charted over `Ω`, with maps `uᵢ : W ⟶ Y`.
  Suppose that `∑ mᵢ [Frob^{aᵢ}(uᵢ x)] = 0` at the field-valued points `x` of the special fibre of
  `W`. Suppose also that each `γᵢ` in the decomposition group acts on the residue field as
  `x ↦ x ^ (1/p^aᵢ)`. Then `∑ mᵢ uᵢ^* ∘ linearFrob(γᵢ, aᵢ) = 0` on `Bmax ⊗ Vⁿ(Y)`.
* `New.Variety.exists_hasHodgeTateWeight`: let `Y` be proper, smooth of relative dimension `d` and
  charted over `Ω`. Let `E` be a field between `R` and `Ω`, and let `E → k → ℚ̄_p` be compatible,
  with a section `ε` of `k → ℚ̄_p`. Fix `h`, a proper `W`, and a class `x` in degree-`q` Hodge
  cohomology of `Y` over `E`. Then there are `v` in `ℂ_p ⊗ V^(q+h)(Y)` and an `ε`-semilinear map `Θ`
  with two properties. First, `v` has Hodge–Tate weight `h` for the decomposition group over `E`.
  Second, `hodgeTateMap h (u^* x) = Θ(u^* v)` for every `u : W ⟶ Y`.

These replace the primitive, crystalline and Hodge–Tate comparison theorems (Faltings, Scholze,
Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze) as used in `Lib.Shimura.Eigenspace`. There is no integral form, no Hodge–Tate
decomposition, and no identification with étale or crystalline cohomology.

`Descent` defines the test rings and proves acyclicity for almost coefficients. `Duality` on powers
of `ℙ¹`, with `Lib.Cohomology.SmoothBaseChange`, extends the comparison from a point to `Y`.
`Primitive` deduces the first result and lifts it to periods by `Completion`; the map is in
`HodgeTate.PeriodMap`. `Crystalline` uses `ToricTower` (roots of one unit at a time) for the
crystalline statement, and `CrystallineFrobenius` treats Frobenius. `HodgeTate` builds the
Hodge–Tate map.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.exists_cancels_frobPow_locally`: if p divides a power of z and a fixed power of z
  divides the image of 𝔴, then near each maximal ideal of a test the relation holds modulo z.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.Cancels`: the integers m_i add up to zero on every fibre of a family v_i, that is, Σ
  m_i [v_i] = 0 in the free abelian group on the v_i.
* `New.Variety.CongruenceRelation`: Σ m_i [F_i u_i(x)] = 0 (`New.Variety.Cancels`) for every point x
  of W in a field of characteristic p that kills 𝔴, where F_i is the a_i-th iterate of Frobenius.
* `New.Period.Bmax`: The period ring B = B^+[1/μ] (Colmez's B_max, not Fontaine's B_cris), over
  which crystalline representations are defined.
* `New.Period.linearFrob`: β_{s,m}: a chosen B-linear endomorphism of B⊗T agreeing with φ^m
  j(s) ⊗ ρ(s) on D_pcris(T), if one exists (arbitrary otherwise).
modules.literature:
Known result: Congruence relation for the crystalline Frobenius. In the literature, characteristic
polynomials are compared through cycle classes. Here a relation among Frobenius twists of maps,
given on points of the special fibre, is carried directly to a relation among operators on
crystalline invariants. Source: Scholl, Motives for modular forms, 1990, Invent. Math. 100, §4.2.3,
through Katz–Messing, Some consequences of the Riemann hypothesis for varieties over finite fields,
1974, Invent. Math. 23, Thm 2(2); for the ramified base, Berthelot–Ogus, F-isocrystals and de Rham
cohomology I, 1983, Invent. Math. 72.

modules.title: Divided power envelopes, lifts modulo divided powers, and one divided power variable
modules.note:
For a prime `p` (fixed by the class `New.ThePrime p`) and a `p`-torsion-free, `p`-adically
complete ring `S` (`New.Variety.IsCompleteTorsionFree`), `New.Variety.pdIdeal S` is the ideal of the
`x` with `n ! ∣ x ^ n` for all `n`. The file proves lifting results along `S → S ⧸ pdIdeal S`. It
then constructs the divided power envelope of a subset `J` of `T` and proves its universal property.
Finally it treats one divided power variable `z = t - v`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.IsCompleteTorsionFree.monoidHom_lift_bijective`,
  `New.Variety.IsCompleteTorsionFree.existsUnique_witt_lift`: multiplicative maps from a perfect
  monoid, and ring maps from a perfect ring via its Witt vectors, lift uniquely from `S ⧸ pdIdeal S`
  to `S`.
* `New.Variety.IsCompletionBijective.comp_bijective`: maps to a `p`-complete ring extend uniquely
  along a map that is bijective modulo every power of `p` (`New.Variety.IsCompletionBijective`).
* `New.Variety.preEnvelope`, `New.Variety.Envelope`: adjoin the `x ^ n / n !`, `x ∈ J`, inside
  `T ⊗ ℚ`, then complete; `New.Variety.Envelope.existsUnique_lift` is the universal property.
* `New.Variety.exists_preEnvelope_basis`: if `T` has the `B`-basis `u a * v ^ n`, the uncompleted
  envelope of `z = t - v` has the basis `u a * z ^ n / n !`.
* `New.Variety.koszulExact_pd_line`: take an endomorphism `γ` that scales the unit `v` by `1 + q`
  with `p ^ 3 ∣ q`. It must also scale each `u a` with `a ≠ 0` by `1 + η` with `p * η ∣ q`, and
  `u 0 = 1`. Then the sequence `0 → B → E → E → 0` given by `γ - 1` is exact after a base change
  that inverts `q`. The proof uses a shift `S` of the basis such that `(γ - 1) S` is `q * v` times
  `1 - p W` for an endomorphism `W`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.CrysTest`: the category of `p`-torsion-free, `p`-adically complete `S`-algebras
  (`New.Variety.IsCompleteTorsionFree`); an object `E` is read as its underlying ring.
* `New.Variety.KoszulExact`: for a map `i` and an endomorphism `g`, the map `i` is injective, every
  fixed point of `g` lies in the image of `i`, and `z ↦ g z - z` is onto.

modules.title: Crystalline comparison: bijectivity on étale charts and spanning of period cohomology
modules.note:
Write A_inf = `New.Period.Ainf`, A_max = `New.Period.Amax`, B_max = `New.Period.Bmax`, and 𝔡(B) =
`New.Variety.pdIdeal` B for the ideal of the x with n! ∣ x^n for all n. Here ξ = `New.Period.xi`
generates the kernel of θ : A_inf → O_C. Fix an action of A_inf on A_max satisfying
`New.Variety.CrysPeriodAlgebra`. For a functor P on O_C-algebras, the crystalline comparison
compares two cohomologies. The first is that of D ↦ P(D/𝔡(D)) on p-torsion-free p-complete
A_max-algebras D, with coefficients B_max ⊗ D. The second is that of P on p-adic tests. Finally, let
S be a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser p, let O_C be an algebra over a ring R with
a map R → S/𝔡(S), let A_max be an S-algebra, and assume a given natural map from D ↦ D/𝔡(D) (as
R-algebras via O_C → A_max/𝔡(A_max)) to D ↦ D/𝔡(D) (via R → S/𝔡(S)) on p-torsion-free p-complete
A_max-algebras is an isomorphism; let V be a subfunctor of a functor X on R-algebras with
`New.Variety.IsCharting` V (V covers X and is built from charts étale over tori). Then the classes
pulled back from D ↦ V(D/𝔡) on p-torsion-free p-complete S-algebras span the period cohomology of V
over B_max when it is finite.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.CrysPeriodAlgebra`: the properties of an A_inf-algebra structure on A_max that the
  comparison needs.
* `New.Variety.exists_crysPeriodAlgebra`: for each y in O_C with p ∣ y^N, there is an algebra
  structure as in `New.Variety.CrysPeriodAlgebra` that is equivariant for Frobenius and Galois and
  whose map O_C → A_max/𝔡(A_max) kills y.
* `New.Variety.HasCrysComparison`: the comparison along `New.Variety.crysThickening` and
  `New.Variety.testToPdReduction` is bijective in every degree.
* `New.Variety.hasCrysComparison_of_witt`, `New.Variety.hasCrysComparison_of_etale`:
  `New.Variety.HasCrysComparison` holds for P = Hom_{A_inf}(T, −), with scalars restricted from O_C
  to A_inf, when the A_inf-algebra T maps to W(b), for a perfect π-torsion-free O^♭-algebra b, by a
  map bijective on p-adic completions. It also holds for P = Hom(B, −) with B étale over O_C[G],
  where G is a ℚ≥0-module.
* `New.Variety.hasCrysComparison_chart`: the comparison holds for Hom_R(B, −) on O_C-algebras when B
  is étale over R[X_1, …, X_d], each X_i going to a unit t_i. Adjoining all roots of the t_i reduces
  it to `New.Variety.hasCrysComparison_of_etale`.
* `New.Variety.span_range_crysComparison_pull_eq_top`: for S a complete discrete valuation ring with
  uniformiser p, the classes pulled back from the cohomology of D ↦ V(D/𝔡) span the period
  cohomology of V over B_max when it is finite.

Notions from other files:
* `New.OC`: The ring of integers O_C of the field C_p of p-adic complex numbers.
* `New.Period.OFlat`: The ring O^♭, the inverse limit of O_C/p along x ↦ x^p;
  π = p♭ = `New.Variety.pFlat` is ξ mod p, the zeroth Witt coefficient of ξ.
* `New.Variety.PadicTest`: A p-adic test: a non-empty family of cells (`New.Variety.IsCell`) with a
  ring map from O_C to their product S (`ProdRing`); S^♭ is the tilt of S and θ : W(S^♭) → S is
  Fontaine's map.
* `New.Period.Amax`: Colmez's period ring A_max, the p-adic completion of A_inf[X]/(pX − ξ).
* `New.Variety.compatibleRoots`: The functor of characters ℚ≥0 → A on O_C-algebras A, with the twist
  by s ↦ (ε^s)^♯ as an endomorphism (a functor on O_C-algebras × Bℕ, `New.Variety.TimesBNat`).
* `New.Variety.IsLine`: A map Y → U from a functor with an endomorphism is a line if the cohomology
  of U maps bijectively to that of Y on the product with Bℕ.
modules.literature:
Known result: Crystalline comparison for p-adic étale cohomology with good reduction. Only
crystallinity is proved here. It is for cohomology on p-adic test rings, which is not identified
with étale cohomology. There is no filtration and no identification with crystalline cohomology.
Invariants come from p-complete torsion-free rings modulo elements with divided powers, and they are
compared on toric towers one coordinate at a time. Source: Bhatt, Morrow, Scholze, Integral p-adic
Hodge theory, 2018, Publ. IHÉS 128, Thm 1.1(i) (first proved in Faltings, Crystalline cohomology and
p-adic Galois representations, 1989); for the site, Bhatt, Prismatic F-gauges, 2022, Rem. 2.5.12;
for the line lemma, Andreatta–Brinon, Acyclicité géométrique de B_cris relatif, 2013, Comment. Math.
Helv. 88.

modules.title: Divided power ideal, p-adic test rings, tilt, Witt vectors and reduction modulo p
modules.note:
This file sets up basic objects of the p-adic and crystalline comparison, for a prime p.
O_C = `New.OC` is the ring of integers of ℂ_p, O♭ = `New.Period.OFlat` is its tilt, and
ξ = `New.Period.xi` generates ker θ in A_inf = W(O♭). The prime p is implicit in `New.Period.OFlat`
and `New.Period.xi`. The file defines the ideal 𝔡(S) of the x with n! ∣ x^n for all n, and
categories of p-complete p-torsion-free test rings. Finally, it collects the commutative algebra of
flatness, reduction modulo an element and Witt vectors that is used throughout the p-adic
comparison.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.pdIdeal`: the ideal 𝔡(S) of the x with n! ∣ x^n for all n.
  `New.Variety.pdIdeal_le_comap`: ring maps send 𝔡(B) into 𝔡(k).
* `New.Variety.IsCompleteTorsionFree` and `New.Variety.CrysTest`: p-torsion-free p-complete rings,
  and the category of such S-algebras. `New.Variety.CrysTest.restrictScalars` restricts scalars.
* `New.Variety.baseChangeMap`, `New.Variety.HasFlatBaseChange`: the map M ⊗ H^n(N, Φ) → H^n(N,
  M ⊗ Φ), and the statement that it is bijective for flat M.
* `New.Variety.IsCell`, `New.Variety.PadicTest`: cells, and p-adic tests, which are non-empty
  products S of cells with a map from O_C = `New.OC`.
* `New.Variety.PadicTest.tilt`, `New.Variety.algCompletion`, `New.Variety.wittFunctor`,
  `New.Variety.periodAlg`: tilt, p-adic completion, Witt vectors, and the completion of T ⊗ W(b)
  over A_inf.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.Comparison`: A comparison from F on C to F' on C': a functor φ: C' → C with a natural
  transformation β: F∘φ → F'.

modules.title: p-adic tests: tilts, Fontaine's map, covers by tests and flat base change
modules.note:
A cell is a p-complete, absolutely integrally closed valuation ring in which p is neither zero nor a
unit. A p-adic test c is a non-empty product S = `c.ProdRing` of cells over O_C. Its tilt is
S♭ = `c.TiltRing`. ξ generates the kernel of Fontaine's map θ : W(S♭) → S, and
π = `New.Variety.pFlat` is ξ mod p. The file computes the tilt and the kernel of θ for tests. For
perfect b, it identifies algebra maps b → S♭ with algebra maps O_C ⊗ W(b) → S (`wittFunctor` sends b
to W(b) over A_inf, and `algBaseChange OC` is O_C ⊗_{A_inf} –), so tilting is fully faithful on
tests. It also produces cells over primes and covers by tests, and proves flat base change for
ℤ[Y∘ι], for ι full, faithful and with covering points, when Y is affinely covered.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.PadicTest.tiltPiEquiv`, `New.Variety.PadicTest.isPerfectTorsionFree_tilt`: S♭ is the
  product of the tilts of the cells; it is perfect and has no π-torsion.
* `New.Variety.PadicTest.ker_theta`: the kernel of Fontaine's θ : W(S♭) → S is generated by ξ.
* `New.Variety.PadicTest.thetaIso`: O_C ⊗_{A_inf} W(S♭) ≅ S, naturally in the test.
* `New.Variety.homTiltIso`: for perfect `b`, algebra maps `b → c.TiltRing` correspond to algebra
  maps `O_C ⊗ W(b) → c.ProdRing` by `f ↦ θ ∘ W(f)`, naturally in the test `c`.
* `New.Variety.hasCoveringPoints_padic`: if an algebra has a point in some test, then all its points
  in tests factor through a single point.
* `New.Variety.IsAffinelyCovered.hasFlatBaseChange`, `New.Variety.hasFlatBaseChange_of_iso_reprBy`:
  ℤ[Y∘ι] has flat base change (`New.Variety.HasFlatBaseChange`: its base change maps are bijective
  in all degrees) for affinely covered Y, when ι is full, faithful and has covering points. ℤ[Y] has
  flat base change for Y isomorphic to the points of an O_C-algebra.

Notions from other files:
* `New.OC`: The ring of integers O_C of the field C_p of p-adic complex numbers.
* `New.Variety.PadicTest.algFunctor`: The functor from p-adic tests to commutative O_C-algebras
  sending a test to its product ring S with its structure map; `reprBy B` is the functor of points
  R ↦ (algebra maps B → R), and `Sigma F` is the type of pairs (c, point of `F c`).
* `New.Variety.freeAb`: The functor sending a set-valued functor Y to Z[Y], whose value at A is the
  free abelian group on Y(A).
* `New.Variety.IsAffinelyCovered`: `X` is separated and, after restriction along `ι`, covered by one
  affine: there are a `k`-algebra `B` and a point `y` of `X(B)` such that, for every object `c`,
  each point of `X(ι c)` is the image of `y` under some map `B → ι c`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Tilting and untilting for products of perfectoid valuation rings over O_C. Only
products of p-complete absolutely integrally closed valuation rings over O_C are treated, and such a
ring is recovered from the Witt vectors of its tilt. Tilting is fully faithful, and maps from a
perfect algebra to the tilt are maps from its untilt. Source: B. Bhatt, M. Morrow, P. Scholze,
Integral p-adic Hodge theory, Publ. Math. IHES 128 (2018), Lemma 3.10; P. Scholze, Perfectoid
spaces, Publ. Math. IHES 116 (2012), Theorem 5.2.

See also `Lib.PadicComparison.Descent.AlmostDescent` and `Lib.Cohomology.Etale.FilteredLimits`.

modules.title: Almost coefficients, v-descent for perfect algebras and acyclicity of tilt points
modules.note:
The tilt O♭ (`New.Period.OFlat`) has maximal ideal 𝔪 (`New.Variety.MaxIdealFlat`) and contains p♭
(`New.Variety.pFlat`); N is an O♭-module killed by p♭. The coefficient functor
`New.Variety.almostCoeff N` sends an O♭-algebra b to b ⊗ N ⊗ 𝔪, a case of
`New.Variety.tensorCoeff`.
For these coefficients, a map of perfect O♭-algebras that is onto on points in tilts of tests is a
cover. By Čech descent, the points of a perfect algebra in tilts are acyclic. Auxiliary results
treat 𝔪² = 𝔪 and Witt vectors of O♭-algebras.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.isCover_of_points`: if p^♭ kills N, a map b → b' of perfect O^♭-algebras that is onto
  on points with values in tilts of tests is a cover (`New.Variety.IsCover`) for the coefficients
  D ↦ D ⊗ N ⊗ 𝔪.
* `New.Variety.isAcyclicAt_perfectTilt`: for N killed by p♭, the points of a perfect O♭-algebra in
  tilts of tests are acyclic (`New.Variety.IsAcyclicAt`) for the coefficients b ↦ b ⊗ N ⊗ 𝔪. This
  holds on the category of perfect O♭-algebras.
* `New.Variety.isAcyclicOnPerfect_almostCoeff`: the same on all O♭-algebras, for b perfect.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Period.OFlat`: The ring O^♭, the inverse limit of O_C/p along x ↦ x^p, where O_C is the ring
  of integers of C_p.
* `New.Variety.moduleCoeff`, `New.Variety.tensorWith`: A functor Φ to S-modules regarded as
  coefficients for cohomology, and M ⊗_S Φ for an S-module M.
* `New.Variety.pFlat`: The element p^♭ = ξ mod p of O^♭ = A_inf/p, the zeroth Witt coefficient of
  the generator ξ of the kernel of θ.
* `New.Variety.PadicTest`: A non-empty family of cells (`New.Variety.IsCell`) with a ring map from
  O_C = `New.OC` to their product; `TiltRing` is the tilt of the product.
modules.literature:
Known result: Almost acyclicity of the structure sheaf for the v-topology. The statement holds for
any perfect algebra over the tilt of O_C, as cohomology on products of complete absolutely
integrally closed valuation rings modulo p♭, with the maximal ideal put into the coefficients so
that the result is exact. The proof passes to a valuation ring. Source: P. Scholze, Étale cohomology
of diamonds, arXiv 1709.07343 (2017), Theorem 8.7, Proposition 8.8; for perfect rings B. Bhatt, P.
Scholze, Projectivity of the Witt vector affine Grassmannian, Invent. Math. 209 (2017), Theorem 4.1;
points argument O. Gabber, S. Kelly, Points in algebraic geometry, J. Pure Appl. Algebra 219 (2015),
Theorem 2.3.

modules.title: Integration over ℙ¹, compared cohomology theories, and moving kernel classes in (ℙ¹)^d
modules.group: Duality and good pairs for compared theories
modules.note:
The file gives the geometric step of the duality for a zero locus in (ℙ¹)^d: a kernel class is moved
between points one coordinate at a time. In the first section, g is a functor from C to tests over
A, ℓ is invertible in A, and I is a family of ideals on the points of a functor X on tests. η
denotes the class `New.Variety.etaClass`; `M.HasLineFormula` (the projective line formula) says
that, for every S, each class from S over the points of ℙ¹ is a·1 + b·η for unique a, b restricted
from the base. The file then sets up the formal comparison of two cohomology theories on tests over
`A`, using integration over `ℙ¹`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.IdealFamily.exists_move_kernel`: a class at the point t(q) is moved to t(q') by
  multiplying with the classes η(q_j) + η(q'_j).
* `New.Variety.TorsionCoeff.HasLineFormula.integrate`: integration `a + η b ↦ b` over `ℙ¹`, given
  `New.Variety.TorsionCoeff.HasLineFormula`.
* `New.Variety.ComparedTheory`, `New.Variety.ComparedTheory.IsFiniteLerayHirsch`: a theory with maps
  from the locally constant `ZMod ℓ` coefficients, and the property that these maps compute its
  cohomology from finite groups.
* `New.Variety.NaturalOp`: operations on cohomology, natural in the theory, with parameters in `ℙ¹`.
* `New.Variety.ComparedTheory.isClosedClass_isFiniteLerayHirsch`,
  `New.Variety.ComparedTheory.isFiniteLerayHirsch_of_shortExact`,
  `New.Variety.ComparedTheory.isFiniteLerayHirsch_iff_of_isCohomEquiv`,
  `New.Variety.ComparedTheory.isFiniteLerayHirsch_of_retract`: the property passes along short exact
  sequences, equivalences and retracts by operations.
* `New.Variety.ComparedTheory.isFiniteLerayHirsch_of_integrate_params`,
  `New.Variety.ComparedTheory.isFiniteLerayHirsch_topPoints_of_surjective`: it passes to pairs in
  `(ℙ¹)^m`, by self-duality.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.TestOver`: The category of tests over A: the full subcategory of commutative
  A-algebras whose underlying rings are test rings.
* `New.Variety.TorsionCoeff`: a functor F on C to abelian groups, killed by ℓ, with Zariski descent
  for the rings g(c). A `New.Variety.Theory` is one that also behaves well on closed loci.
* `New.Variety.IdealFamily`: For a functor ι from C to commutative rings, ideals I_c of ι(c) such
  that I_b is generated by the image of I_a for every morphism a → b.
* `New.Variety.IdealFamily.topLocus`: the subfunctor of the one-point functor that is non-empty
  exactly where I_c is the unit ideal.

modules.title: Good pairs: excision, Thom retraction and Alexander duality for principal opens
modules.group: Duality and good pairs for compared theories
modules.note:
Spaces are set-valued functors on the tests over `A` (`New.Variety.TestOver`, the full subcategory
of `A`-algebras satisfying `IsTest`). A pair `(Y, U)` is the functor
`New.Variety.relFreeAb U = ℤ[Y] / ℤ[U]`. The pair is good,
`New.Variety.ComparedTheory.IsFiniteLerayHirsch D`, if its cohomology with locally constant
`ℤ/ℓ`-coefficients is finite and compares bijectively with the theory `D`. Here
`New.Variety.offClosedFibre Y` is the part of `Y` on tests where the maximal ideal of `A` generates
the unit ideal.

* `New.Variety.ComparedTheory.isFiniteLerayHirsch_iff_of_locally_bijective`: excision along a map
  that is Zariski-locally bijective on pairs.
* `New.Variety.ComparedTheory.isFiniteLerayHirsch_of_prod_projLine`: goodness descends from the
  product with `(ℙ¹, ℙ¹ ∖ (0 : 1))`.
* `New.Variety.ComparedTheory.isFiniteLerayHirsch_principal_open`: principal opens of affine space
  inside `(ℙ¹)^d`, by Alexander duality.
* `New.Variety.ComparedTheory.isFiniteLerayHirsch_standard_etale`: standard étale charts, by two
  excisions.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.projLine.unimodularRow`: homogeneous coordinates (1 + uv, v) of a point of P¹(B) with
  chosen representative (u, v); `New.Variety.projLine.affinePt x` is the point (x : 1).
* `New.Variety.ComparedTheory`: a theory along g with morphisms to its coefficient from the locally
  constant ℤ/ℓ-valued functions, such that it and `New.Variety.Theory.locallyConstant` satisfy the
  projective line formula.
* `New.Variety.IsZariskiLocallyTop ι U`: every point of `Y` lies in `U` after inverting some element
  outside any given maximal ideal, that is, `U` is all of `Y` Zariski-locally.
modules.literature:
Known result: Comparison of cohomology theories by duality, via a diagonal kernel on products of P¹.
This step is common to several comparison theorems. It concerns torsion coefficient theories in
which the projective line is computed. In these theories, a class supported on the diagonal of
(P¹)^d carries finiteness and comparison from the point to standard étale charts over affine space.
Sources for the theorems: SGA 4 XVI, SGA 4½ Finitude/Dualité; Faltings, Scholze primitive
comparison. The proof is in the spirit of Dold–Puppe dualisability.

modules.title: Ext¹ classes of cocycles of functors, and contraction on exterior algebras
modules.group: The Hodge–Tate map and Hodge–Tate weights
modules.note:
For functors `N`, `F` from `C` to abelian groups (`New.Variety.AbFunctor C`),
`New.Variety.TotalH N F = ⨁ₙ Extⁿ(N, F)` is the total Ext group. Its Yoneda product is
`New.Variety.TotalH.comp x y`, with `x` first. A morphism `f` gives the class
`New.Variety.TotalH.homClass f` of degree 0, and `New.Variety.TotalH.map Φ` applies an exact functor
`Φ` degree by degree. The file proves a sign rule for connecting classes and attaches to a 1-cocycle
a class in `Ext¹`. For a semilinear map `φ = (φ₀, φ₁) : M → T' × M'`, it also defines
`New.Variety.contraction φ : ⋀ M → ⋀ M'`, which contracts with `φ₀` and applies `φ₁` to the
remaining factors, and proves a product rule for it.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.TotalH.extClass_sign_comm`: the connecting classes of a short exact sequence of
  functors `Ψ → Ξ → Φ` commute with a class of degree `a` up to the sign `(-1) ^ a`.
* `New.Variety.Cocycle`, `New.Variety.Cocycle.cohomClass`: a 1-cocycle from `F` to `G` twists
  `G × F` into an extension of `F` by `G`, hence a class in `Ext¹(F, G)`.
* `New.Variety.contraction_mul`: `New.Variety.contraction φ` is a graded derivation along
  `New.Variety.exteriorMapSnd φ`, the ring map of `φ₁`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.abTensor`: The pointwise tensor product over ℤ of two such functors, as a bifunctor.
* `New.Variety.restrictAlong`: For φ: C' → C, the functor N ↦ N∘φ from functors on C to functors on
  C', with values in D.

modules.title: The ring R[1/p] of a p-adic test and the square-zero extension W(R♭)[1/p]/(ker θ)²
modules.group: The Hodge–Tate map and Hodge–Tate weights
modules.note:
Let `c` be a p-adic test with ring R = `c.ProdRing`, a product of valuation rings over O_C. Put K =
R[1/p] (`New.Variety.PadicTest.GenericRing`) and B = W(R♭)[1/p]/(ker θ)², where θ is Fontaine's map.
Since p is not a zero divisor in R, the map R → K is injective. B is a square-zero extension of K by
K, and the map ℚ̄_p → K lifts uniquely to B over ℤ_p. Both constructions are functorial in `c`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.genericOver`, `New.Variety.thickeningOver`: `c ↦ K` and `c ↦ B` as functors to
  `k`-algebras.
* `New.Variety.thickeningOver.exact_mulMu_proj`: `0 → K → B → K → 0` is exact; the first map comes
  from multiplication by `μ` (`New.Period.mu`).
* `New.Variety.exists_periodAlg_iso_genericAlg`, `New.Variety.hasZariskiDescent_genericOver`: `K` as
  a completed tensor product; Zariski descent.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.PadicTest.TiltRing`: The tilt R♭, the inverse limit of R/p along Frobenius.
* `New.Period.Ainf`: The ring A_inf of p-typical Witt vectors over the tilt O♭ of O_C.

modules.title: The Hodge–Tate maps λ_h on pairs (S, M): construction, properties and restriction
modules.group: The Hodge–Tate map and Hodge–Tate weights
modules.note:
The field `k` is embedded in `ℚ̄_p`, so it has characteristic zero. For a `p`-adic test `S`, put
`T = S[1/p]`, and let `B_S = W(S^♭)[1/p] / (ker θ)²` be the square-zero extension
`New.Variety.thickeningOver` of `T` by `T`.
Put `B_{S,M} = B_S ×_T (T ⊕ M)`. All groups are `Ext` groups of functors to abelian groups
(`New.Variety.H`). On pairs `(S, M)` with `M = T ^ n`, the Hodge–Tate map `λ_h` restricts a Hodge
class to the pairs. It then composes it with the `h`-th Yoneda power of the class of a contraction
cocycle, followed by the projection to degree zero. So `λ_h` lands in the cohomology of `N(B_{S,M})`
on pairs. This map is natural, turns scaling by `t` into multiplication by `t ^ h`, and satisfies a
binomial product rule.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.HodgeTatePair`: pairs `(S, M)` with `M = T ^ n`; a map has a semilinear part
  `M → T' × M'`.
* `New.Variety.HodgeTatePair.contractionPow`: the `h`-th Yoneda power of the class of the
  contraction cocycle `New.Variety.HodgeTatePair.contractionCocycle`, followed by the projection to
  degree zero. It is `k`-linear (`New.Variety.HodgeTatePair.act_comp_contractionPow`)
  and has weight `h` (`New.Variety.HodgeTatePair.scaleModule_comp_contractionPow`).
* `New.Variety.hodgeTateMap`: restrict a class of `New.Variety.HodgeH` to these pairs and compose
  with `contractionPow h`. `New.Variety.restrictToPairs` maps the degree-`n` cohomology of `N(T)` on
  `p`-adic tests to the same target `New.Variety.PairH`.
* `New.Variety.PairRestrictBijective`: restriction along `B_{S,M} → T` is bijective on cohomology in
  all degrees.
* `New.Variety.PairRestrictBijective.exists_hodgeTateMap_eq`: under this hypothesis,
  `hodgeTateMap h x` for `x` of degree `q` comes from a class of degree `q + h`.
* `New.Variety.IsChartCovered.pairRestrictBijective`: `PairRestrictBijective` holds for `ℤ[X]` if
  `X` is covered by étale charts. The map `B_{S,M} → T` is a square-zero extension
  (`New.Variety.HodgeTatePair.isSquareZero_toGeneric`), so the lifts of a point of a chart of
  dimension `n` are represented by one pair `(S, T ^ n)`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.PadicTest`: a p-adic test, a non-empty family of cells (`New.Variety.IsCell`) with a
  ring map from O_C to their product.
* `New.Variety.Cocycle`: a 1-cocycle from F to G, homomorphisms D(f): F(c) → G(d) for f: c → d, with
  D(gf) = G(g)D(f) + D(g)F(f); `D.cohomClass` is its class in Ext¹(F, G).
* `New.Variety.contraction`: for semilinear φ = (φ₀, φ₁): M → T' × M', the map ⋀M → ⋀M' that
  contracts with φ₀ and applies φ₁.
* `New.Variety.TotalH`: the total Ext group, the direct sum of the Ext^n(N,F) over all n ≥ 0;
  `comp x y` is the Yoneda product, `x` followed by `y`.
* `New.Variety.HodgeH`: Hodge cohomology of a functor N on k-algebras, Ext^q from (A, M) ↦ N(A ⊕ M)
  to (A, M) ↦ ⋀_A M on pairs of a k-algebra A and a free module M = A^ι.

modules.title: Galois twists and the weight of the Hodge–Tate map
modules.group: The Hodge–Tate map and Hodge–Tate weights
modules.note:
An element `g` of `Gal(ℚ̄_p/ℚ_p)` twists a p-adic test `c` by precomposing its structure map
`O_C → R` with `g` (`New.Variety.PadicTest.twist`). The twist leaves the rings `R`, `K = R[1/p]` and
`B = W(R♭)[1/p] / (ker θ)²` unchanged. Write `μ = [ε] − 1` and `χ` for the cyclotomic character.
Suppose `g` fixes `E` and `New.Variety.restrictToPairs ξ` is the image under
`New.Variety.hodgeTateMap h` of a Hodge class defined over `E`, and that `χ(g⁻¹)` is the image in
ℚ̄_p of some `t : k`. Then the twist by `g` multiplies `New.Variety.restrictToPairs ξ` by
`χ(g⁻¹)^h`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.thickeningOver.mulMu_twist`: the inclusion `ι : K → B` (multiplication by `μ`)
  changes by the cyclotomic character `χ(g⁻¹)` (`New.cyclotomicGp`), as `g⁻¹ μ ≡ χ(g⁻¹) μ` modulo
  `μ²`.
* `New.Variety.HodgeTatePair.galTwist`: the twist on pairs `(c, K^n)` (`New.Variety.HodgeTatePair`).
* `New.Variety.HodgeTatePair.contractionPow_galTwist`: the classes
  `New.Variety.HodgeTatePair.contractionPow` (the `h`-th power of the contraction class, then the
  projection to degree zero) are compatible with the twist.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.PadicTest`: A p-adic test: a non-empty family of cells (`New.Variety.IsCell`) with a
  ring map from O_C to their product R.
* `New.Variety.thickeningOver.mulMu`: The additive map ι: K → B sending θ(x) to the class of μx,
  where μ = [ε] − 1.
* `New.Variety.HodgeTatePair`: A pair (S,M) of a p-adic test S and a free module M of finite rank
  over T = S[1/p]; `New.Variety.HodgeTatePair.pairAlg` sends it to B_{S,M} = B_S ×_T (T ⊕ M).
* `New.Variety.hodgeTateMap`: The map λ_h: restrict a Hodge class along B_{S,M} → T ⊕ M, apply the
  h-th power of the contraction class, and project ⋀M to degree zero.
* `New.Variety.restrictToPairs`: Restriction along B_{S,M} → T, from the cohomology of N(T) on
  p-adic tests S to that of N(B_{S,M}) on pairs. `New.Variety.PairRestrictBijective` says that it is
  bijective in all degrees.

modules.title: The period map for ℓ-adic cohomology on p-adic tests, and Hodge–Tate weights
modules.group: The Hodge–Tate map and Hodge–Tate weights
modules.note:
This file compares the geometric cohomology `New.Variety.ellAdicCohom R Ω n` of an `R`-scheme `Y`
(`Ω` an `R`-algebra on which a group `Γ` acts by ring maps fixing the image of `R`), written
`V^n(Y)`, with the cohomology of the points of `Y` in `p`-adic tests. A vector has weight `h`
(`New.HasHodgeTateWeight`) if Galois acts on it by the `(-h)`-th power of the cyclotomic character.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.toTwistAlg`: the identity of a `p`-adic test as an `R`-algebra map to its Galois
  twist.
* `New.Variety.exists_period_map`: the period map is natural, Galois equivariant, and bijective for
  proper charted `Y`. It is the pull-back along the comparison of
  `New.Variety.exists_primitive_period_comparison`.
* `New.Variety.exists_hasHodgeTateWeight`: the value of the Hodge–Tate map on a Hodge class comes
  from a vector of weight `h`, naturally in maps to `Y`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.PadicTest`: A p-adic test c: a non-empty family of cells, whose product is the ring
  `c.ProdRing`, with a ring map from O_C, the integers of ℂ_p, to that product.
* `New.Variety.PadicTest.twist`: For g in G_p, the endofunctor of p-adic tests that keeps the ring
  and precomposes its structure map O_C → c.ProdRing with the action of g.
modules.literature:
Known result: The primitive comparison theorem and the period isomorphism. Here coefficients are
constant, schemes are proper and charted (`New.Variety.IsCharted`), cohomology is taken on test
rings, and the maximal ideal is put into the coefficients. The result is deduced from the duality
comparison on products of projective lines, without almost finiteness. Source: P. Scholze, p-adic
Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Forum Math. Pi 1 (2013), Thm 1.3 and 5.1; for the method,
B. Zavyalov, Poincaré duality in abstract 6-functor formalisms, arXiv 2301.03821, Thm 3.3.3 and
Appl. 1.3.4; Li–Reinecke–Zavyalov, arXiv 2410.08200, §6.4.

Known result: The Hodge–Tate map from Hodge cohomology to p-adic étale cohomology. The target here
is cohomology on test rings, which is not identified with étale cohomology. Only the natural
multiplicative map into the part of weight h is built, from the torsor of lifts modulo the square of
the kernel of Fontaine's map, and bijectivity is not proved. Source: Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory
for rigid-analytic varieties, Forum Math. Pi 1 (2013), Cor. 1.8; the construction follows Bhatt, The
Hodge–Tate decomposition via perfectoid spaces, Arizona Winter School 2017, §3.4.

modules.title: Tilts and period coefficients of p-adic tests: products, comparisons, theories
modules.note:
This file treats the `p`-adic side of the comparison of cohomologies. A `p`-adic test `c`
(`New.Variety.PadicTest`) has a ring `R = c.ProdRing`, a generic ring `R[1/p] = c.GenericRing` and a
tilt `R♭` (`New.Variety.PadicTest.tilt`), an algebra over `O♭ = OFlat`. Here `^` denotes `p`-adic
completion. `S` is an `A_inf`-algebra and `K` is an `S`-algebra.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.bijective_prod_tilt`: bijectivity of `x ↦ (f x, g x)`, which recognises a product,
  passes from the rings of `p`-adic tests to their tilts.
* `New.Variety.IsPeriodRingPair`: `S` is `p`-torsion-free and `p`-complete, `p` divides the image of
  `ξ`, and `τ` is a unit in `K`.
* `New.Variety.hasPartitions_periodAlg`: a functor `Ψ` with an isomorphism `θ` from the period
  coefficients `asModules (tilt ⋙ periodAlg S) ⋙ tensorWith K K` turns a product of two tests into a
  product (`New.Variety.HasPartitions`).
* `New.Variety.CoeffCompBijective.periodAlg_of_almostCoeff`: for an `A_inf`-algebra `S` with
  `IsPeriodRingPair p S K` and `Flat S K`, under base-change hypotheses on `N` and `N'` and with
  `ψ`, `ψ'` perfect and torsion-free, bijectivity of a comparison of cohomology groups
  (`New.Variety.CoeffCompBijective`) passes from the coefficients `b ↦ b ⊗ (O♭ ⊗ S) ⊗ 𝔪`
  (`New.Variety.almostCoeff`) to the coefficients `b ↦ K ⊗ (S ⊗ W(b))^` (`New.Variety.periodAlg`).
  The bridge is the ideal `W(𝔪)` of `A_inf` (`New.Lift.wittOfMaxIdeal`). It reduces to `𝔪` modulo
  `p` and contains `τ` (`New.Period.tau`).
* `New.Variety.primitiveMap`: the `O♭`-algebra map `O♭ ⊗_{𝔽_p} LC(Spec R[1/p]) → R♭` that extends
  `New.Variety.locConstToTilt`, where `LC` denotes locally constant functions.
* `New.Variety.tiltTheory`: with coefficients `R ↦ R♭ ⊗_{O♭} M`, a theory (`New.Variety.Theory`)
  along `New.Variety.genericTestOver`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Period.OFlat`: the ring `O♭`, the inverse limit of `O_C / p` along `x ↦ x ^ p`.
* `New.Variety.IsPerfectTorsionFree b`: the `O♭`-algebra `b` is perfect, and `pFlat`, the class of
  `ξ` modulo `p`, is a non-zero-divisor on it.
* `New.Variety.CoeffCompBijective β α F`: the comparison of cohomology groups along `β` and `α` is
  bijective in every degree for the coefficients `F`.
* `New.Variety.moduleCoeff F`: a functor `F` to modules, read as a functor to abelian groups, to
  serve as coefficients of cohomology.

modules.title: The primitive comparison with period coefficients
modules.note:
The primitive comparison, passed from coefficients modulo `p` to period coefficients. For a `p`-adic
test `c` with ring `R`, let `L` be the ring of locally constant `𝔽_p`-valued functions on
`Spec R[1/p]` (for a test ring `A`, the same ring on `Spec A`; a `p`-adic test gives `A = R[1/p]`).
`New.Variety.primitiveMap` is the natural map of `O♭`-algebras from `O♭ ⊗ L` to the tilt `R♭`; on
`1 ⊗ L` it restricts to `locConstToTilt : L → R♭`, `ℓ ↦ primitiveMap (1 ⊗ ℓ)`. Let `S` be an
`A_inf`-algebra and `K` an `S`-algebra, and let `Ψ` be isomorphic (by `θ`) to the period
coefficients `c ↦ K ⊗ (S ⊗ W(R♭))^`, where `^` is `p`-adic completion.

* `New.Variety.primitivePeriodMap`: the natural map `K ⊗ W(L) → Ψ` induced by
  `New.Variety.primitiveMap`.
* `New.Variety.primitivePeriodMap_isBijective`: this map is bijective on cohomology under several
  conditions. `S` and `K` form a period ring pair, and `K` is flat over `S`. `N` and `N'` have flat
  base change. The cohomology of `N` with coefficients `ℤ_p` is finite over `ℤ_[p]`. The map that
  `New.Variety.primitiveMap` induces on the coefficients `b ↦ b ⊗ (O♭ ⊗ S) ⊗ 𝔪` is bijective on
  cohomology.
* `New.Variety.exists_primitive_period_comparison`: the same, in existential form.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.CoeffCompBijective β α F`: the comparison of cohomology groups along `β` and `α` is
  bijective in every degree for the coefficients `F`.
* `New.Variety.HasFlatBaseChange N`: the cohomology of `N` commutes with flat extension of the
  coefficients.
* `New.Variety.IsPeriodRingPair`: `S` is `p`-torsion-free and `p`-complete, `p` divides the image of
  `ξ` in `S`, and `τ` is a unit in `K`.
* `New.Variety.almostCoeff`: for an `O♭`-module `N`, the functor `b ↦ b ⊗ N ⊗ 𝔪` on `O♭`-algebras,
  `𝔪` the maximal ideal of `O♭`.
* `New.Variety.oFlatLocConst`: the functor from test rings to `O♭`-algebras sending `A` to
  `O♭ ⊗_{𝔽_p} LC(A)`, `LC(A)` the locally constant functions `Spec A → 𝔽_p`.
* `New.Variety.ellAdicCoeff`: the coefficient `ℤ_ℓ` (here `ℓ = p`): a test ring `A` goes to the Witt
  vectors of the ring of locally constant functions `Spec A → 𝔽_ℓ`.

modules.title: The primitive comparison theorem and finiteness of p-adic cohomology
modules.note:
This file concerns a proper scheme `Y` over `R` that is charted over an algebraic closure `Ω` of `ℚ`
(`New.Variety.IsCharted`). A p-adic test is a product of valuation rings over `O_C`, the integers of
`ℂ_p`, and `O^♭` is the tilt of `O_C`. The primitive comparison theorem compares the mod `p`
cohomology of `Y`, tensored with `O^♭`, with the cohomology of its points in p-adic tests with
tilted coefficients.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.finite_and_primitive_comparison`: let `Y` be proper over `R` and charted over `Ω`,
  and assume `IsAcyclicOnPerfect (moduleCoeff (tensorCoeff M))`. Then `Y_Ω` has flat base change and
  finite mod `p` cohomology, and the comparison map is bijective.
* `New.Variety.finite_padic_cohomology`: the cohomology with coefficients `ℤ_p` is finitely
  generated; hence `New.Variety.ellAdicCohom R Ω n`, which is `ℚ_p ⊗` this module, is
  finite-dimensional at `Y`.
* `New.Variety.ellAdicCohom.continuous_galoisAction`: the Galois action
  `New.Variety.ellAdicCohom.galoisAction` is continuous, tested on a vector and a linear map to
  `Q̄_p ^ N`. Modulo `p ^ k` a class is defined over finitely many elements of `Ω`, so it is fixed
  by an open subgroup.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.genericTestOver`: The functor sending a p-adic test with ring R to R[1/p], a test
  over Ω with algebra structure through Ω → ℂ_p.
* `New.Variety.primitiveMap`: The natural map O^♭ ⊗ LC(Spec S[1/p], 𝔽_p) → S^♭ on p-adic tests S,
  with LC the locally constant functions; its source is `New.Variety.oFlatLocConst`.
* `New.Variety.HasFlatBaseChange` N: M ⊗ Hⁿ(N, Φ) → Hⁿ(N, M ⊗ Φ) is bijective for flat M.
* `New.Variety.testPoints`: For R → O_C, the functor sending an R-scheme X to the functor S ↦ X(S)
  of its points over R in p-adic tests.
* `New.Variety.H`: `H N F n` is Extⁿ(N, F) among functors to abelian groups; for
  `N = freeAb X = ℤ[X]` it is the cohomology Hⁿ(X, F). `testIncl ⋙ X` restricts `X` to test rings.
modules.literature:
Known result: Finiteness and Galois continuity of p-adic étale cohomology. The result is stated for
cohomology on test rings, not identified with étale cohomology, of proper schemes charted over an
algebraic closure of Q, with constant coefficients, where integral coefficients are the Witt vectors
of the mod p functions. Finiteness is lifted from finiteness modulo p, which comes from the
primitive comparison. Source: SGA 4, Exp. XIV (Artin), finiteness for proper morphisms; Scholze 2013
Thm 1.1; by duality, Zavyalov arXiv 2301.03821 Appl. 1.3.4.

See also `Lib.PadicComparison.HodgeTate.PeriodMap`.
